segments.text: If Michael Myers is ever standing outside your house... do not look away.
Do not look away. Do not hide in the closet. And never check if he is dead.
This is Protocol four zero four.
There are four rules. Follow them exactly. Otherwise, you will have to activate the emergency protocol.
Rule one. Do not look away.
October thirty-first. Your street is full of masks. Witches. Ghosts. Kids dragging pillowcases full of candy.
But one of them is not moving.
A man in a dark jumpsuit and a pale white mask, standing perfectly still under the streetlight across the street.
He is not looking at the houses. He is looking at your window.
Then he tilts his head. Slowly. Like he is studying you.
Do not look away. Not to call someone. Not to close the curtains. Not even to blink for too long.
He never runs. He does not need to.
Every time you look away, he is a little closer. The streetlight. The mailbox. Your lawn.
And if you look back, and the streetlight is empty...
he is already inside.
Rule two. Count the knives.
Before you go to bed, go to the kitchen. Do not turn on the light. Count the knives in the block.
He never brings his own. He always uses one from your kitchen.
Five slots. Five handles. Good. He is still outside.
But if one slot is empty...
do not look for it. Do not call out. Do not check the other rooms.
He is already inside. And he has your biggest knife.
If you go looking for it, you will find it.
In the reflection of the dark kitchen window. Right behind you.
Rule three. Do not hide in the closet.
You will want to hide in the closet. Everyone does. He knows that.
Through the slats, you can see the hallway. A shape walks past. Slowly. Your kitchen knife in his hand.
He opens every door in the house. One by one. The bathroom. The laundry room. The guest room.
He never hurries. And he always saves the closet for last.
So do not wait for him to reach it. When he walks out of a room, slip into it behind him.
He never checks a room twice.
If you stay in the closet, the last thing you see through the slats will be white.
Rule four. Never check if he is dead.
You might get lucky. A coat hanger. A knitting needle. Your own kitchen knife. He falls.
He lies on the floor. He does not move. The mask is still on.
Do not go closer. Do not check if he is breathing. Do not take the knife out of his hand.
Do not turn your back on him. Walk out of the room backwards, with your eyes on him.
Because the moment you turn around...
behind you, very slowly, he sits up.
He always gets back up.
Emergency protocol. How to fight back.
If he is standing in front of you, and there is nowhere left to go, here is what does not work.
Shoot him. Six times. He falls from the balcony onto the lawn. When you look down, the lawn is empty.
Lock the door. He was inside before you locked it.
Get in the car and drive. In the rearview mirror, there is a white face in the back seat.
Scream. Your neighbors step out onto their porches. They think it is a Halloween prank. They clap.
There is only one thing that works.
Say his name.
Michael.
No one has called him by his name since he was six years old. The knife stops in the air.
Now say it again. The way his mother used to. Calm. Tired.
Michael. Go home.
He tilts his head. He lowers the knife.
Then he turns, walks out of your house, across the street, and into the empty house on the corner. The one nobody has lived in for years.
Do not follow him. Do not watch which window he goes to.
In the morning, the street is quiet. Smashed pumpkins. Candy wrappers. Police tape.
Your kitchen knife is back in the block. Clean.
Every Halloween since, he stands in the dark window of the empty house, and looks at yours.
He never comes over. You told him to go home. He listens to his mother.
But this year, for the first time, he raises his hand.
He is waving.
Do not wave back.
And that was Protocol four zero four.
If this ever happens to you... you know the protocol.
